translations.navDevicesLead: Every paired device and its state
translations.adminOverviewLead: The state of the house in one place: devices, automations and the services behind them.
translations.adminServicesLead: Zigbee, MQTT, Matter and Home Assistant. A service that has not been read yet says so — it is never counted as healthy.
translations.adminAttentionLead: Every device reporting a problem, with the reason it reported. Tap a row to open the device.
translations.adminAttentionEmpty: No device is reporting a problem.
translations.navBackgroundLead: Milky Way, stars and the ridge
translations.skySettingsLead: Only the “By the sun” view uses these, and they stay on this tablet.
translations.skyModeNoticeLead: The moving sky is off right now, so none of this shows on screen.
translations.skyPreviewPlayHint: Runs the whole day in 40 seconds
translations.skyPreviewBadge: preview — tap to return to now
translations.skyPreviewMoonLead: Picking a phase in daylight moves the hour to the middle of the night.
translations.adminModeLead: Setup screens stay locked until the administrator PIN is entered.
translations.adminModeCardLead: One PIN unlocks the setup screens. Everyday controls never ask for it.
translations.adminPinHint: 4 to 8 digits. Wrong entries are slowed down and then locked out.
translations.adminSecretLegacyHint: This installation still uses the old administrator passphrase. Set a PIN below to replace it.
translations.adminPinMismatch: The two PINs do not match.
translations.defaultPinWarningLead: Anyone on this network can open the setup screens. Change it in Settings.
translations.adminModeStripLead: Setup screens are open. Everyday controls are unaffected.
translations.pairingHint: Put the nearby device into pairing mode.

translations.noRoomCardHint: These devices have no room · pick one in Devices
translations.showInOverviewEmpty: It stays out of the overview until a device is added.

translations.hubClockLead: See your cities side by side and keep the list tidy.
translations.hubClockHint: Tap for world clock and alarms
translations.alarmLead: One alarm, kept on this tablet only. It rings here; it does not switch anything on.
translations.noClockCities: No cities selected. Add one using the globe button.
translations.clockCityLimit: You can show up to eight cities.
translations.locationTimezoneUnavailable: This place does not provide time zone information.
translations.chooseWeatherLocationLead: Search for the city whose weather you want to see.
translations.chooseHomeLocationLead: Pick the town your home is in. It is used only to work out sunrise and sunset here on this device.
translations.weatherNoLocationHint: Choose a location to see the weather.
translations.weatherOfflineNote: Offline — showing the last reading from {time}.
translations.deviceTableCount: {count} devices listed — current state only, devices that already left the network are not in this table.
translations.attentionDevicesLead: Disconnected, incomplete or alerting devices appear here.
translations.noExposedControls: This device has no directly adjustable controls.
translations.platformsLead: Open Matter pairing and scan the code in a Matter-compatible controller.
translations.displayNameLead: This name will be shared across all home connections.
translations.nameNewDeviceLead: Choose the name Villa Bridge, Matter and your home platforms will share.
translations.matterLead: Choose “Add Matter device” in Alexa, Apple Home or a compatible Matter controller and scan this code.
translations.matterEcosystemHint: Each ecosystem needs its own code: close this window and press the button again to add another controller such as Alexa.
translations.matterPairingExpired: The pairing window timed out, please try again.
translations.deviceRoleLead: Choose how {name} should appear in Villa Bridge. You can change it later.
translations.chooseDeviceImage: Which one looks like your device?
translations.chooseDeviceImageLead: Choose the closest picture for “{name}”. This only changes how the device looks in Villa Bridge.
translations.useForSameModel: Use this picture automatically for devices with the same model.
translations.pairingCountdown: Put the nearby device into pairing mode · {count} seconds left
translations.stalePageReload: This page was loaded from an old cached copy, so some buttons are inactive. Reload the page.
translations.nameSaved: Name saved. Home platforms will receive it during the next sync.
translations.removeDeviceWarning: This sends a leave command to the physical Zigbee device. It will disappear from Villa Bridge and Matter and must be paired again to return.
translations.forceRemoveLead: If the device no longer responds, force delete removes only its stale coordinator record.
translations.nameMismatch: Type yes to confirm; nothing was removed.
translations.deviceRemoved: Device removed from the Zigbee network.
translations.serverSettingsTitle: You are editing the active server
translations.serverSettingsLead: Zigbee, MQTT and Matter changes are saved on the Villa Bridge server shown in this browser, not locally on this tablet or browser.
translations.adapterUrlHelp: Network coordinator: tcp://address:6638. On a server you can also give a USB path such as /dev/ttyUSB0.
translations.adapterUrlHelpTcpOnly: Network coordinator only: tcp://address:6638. A USB coordinator cannot be used on this device.
translations.adapterManagedByZ2m: Zigbee2MQTT owns this coordinator, so the address is read-only here.
translations.adapterTestNotVerified: Answering is not proof: it does not confirm this is the right coordinator or that it is free to use.
translations.adapterTestActive: This is the coordinator in use right now; it is connected.
translations.adapterTestActiveDegraded: This is the address in use, but the coordinator session is not running.
translations.adapterTestTimeout: No answer from the address in time: {address}
translations.adapterTestDnsFailed: The host name could not be resolved: {address}
translations.adapterTestUnreachable: The address could not be reached: {address}
translations.adapterTestSerialMissing: No serial port at this path: {address}
translations.adapterTestSerialNotDevice: This path is not a serial device: {address}
translations.adapterTestSerialNoAccess: The serial port exists but cannot be opened by the service: {address}
translations.adapterTestRequired: Test the coordinator address before continuing.
translations.adapterTestRequiredHelp: The address is tested before setup continues. A wrong address stops the service from starting and takes the panel with it, and recovery then needs terminal access.
translations.zigbeeAdapterConfirm: Change the coordinator address from {from} to {to}? If the new address is wrong, Villa Bridge will not start again and the panel will not come back; recovery then needs terminal access to the server.
translations.restartNoticeTitle: Changing the channel restarts Villa Bridge
translations.restartNotice: Only a channel change restarts the service; it creates recoverable backups first. Device names and Zigbee network keys are not changed. Automatic repair takes effect right away.
translations.restartConfirm: Save these connection settings and restart Villa Bridge?
translations.settingsSaved: Settings saved. Villa Bridge is restarting…
translations.settingsUnavailable: Connection settings could not be loaded.
translations.restoreStarting: Backup verified. Villa Bridge is restarting…
translations.homeBackupLead: Everything in one file: rooms, device and button names, automations, favourites, notes and the Zigbee network itself. Take one before an update and keep it somewhere safe.
translations.fullBackupKeyWarning: This file contains your Zigbee network key. Keep it private — never e-mail it or upload it to a shared folder.
translations.backupPreparing: Preparing the backup. The file will be saved to your browser's downloads folder.
translations.homeBackupInvalidFile: This is not a valid Villa Bridge home backup.
translations.homeBackupNothing: There is nothing in this file to bring back.
translations.homeBackupSkipped: {count} entries belong to devices that are no longer here, so they will be skipped.
translations.homeBackupNoSkips: Every device in this backup is still in your home.
translations.homeRestoreMergeLead: Bring the backup back and keep anything you have added since.
translations.homeRestoreReplaceLead: Return exactly to the backup. Anything added since it was taken disappears.
translations.homeBackupZigbeeArchiveOnly: The Zigbee part of this backup is Zigbee2MQTT's own archive; it cannot be restored from here.
translations.homeBackupRestartNote: Villa Bridge restarts once because the Zigbee network is being restored.
translations.guidesLead: Run the simple setup again to review the coordinator, MQTT and Matter addresses.
translations.serverGuidesLead: This tablet uses the active Villa Bridge server. Open its setup here.
translations.serverSetupDetectedLead: Villa Bridge is running on the server at {address}. Setup is managed there, so this tablet remains in display-only mode.
translations.serverSetupDetectedHelp: Continue to edit Zigbee, MQTT and Matter on the active server.
translations.setupWelcomeLead: We will prepare your home hub together. Choose the language that feels most comfortable.
translations.setupHubTitle: This tablet is your home hub
translations.setupHubLead: Villa Bridge keeps the essential services together so your home can run without another computer.
translations.setupHubZigbee: Connects your lights, switches and sensors.
translations.setupHubMqtt: Carries device updates securely inside your home.
translations.setupHubMatter: Shares devices with Alexa, Apple Home and other Matter systems.
translations.setupZigbeeLead: This address tells Villa Bridge how to reach the small adapter that talks to your devices.
translations.setupServicesLead: These local addresses connect Zigbee, MQTT and Matter inside Villa Bridge.
translations.setupRecommendedValues: Recommended values are already filled in. Change them only when you use services on another device.
translations.setupNetworkTitle: Keep this tablet easy to find
translations.setupNetworkLead: Home Assistant and other systems use this address to reach Villa Bridge.
translations.setupNetworkHelp: Reserve this address in your router or use Android’s static IP settings so it does not change after a restart.
translations.setupReadyTitle: Congratulations, your home hub is ready
translations.setupReadyLead: We will open Devices next. Add your first Zigbee device there, then build the dashboard you want.
translations.setupSavedRestart: Connection changes were saved. Restart Villa Bridge from Settings when convenient.
translations.finishSetupLead: This device has no name yet. You can pick its name, its room and what it does now.
translations.emptyDevicesLead: Put a Zigbee device into pairing mode, then use the button below. Villa Bridge will guide you through the rest.
translations.tourStatusLead: Lights on, openings and motion stay here at the top, live at a glance.
translations.tourQuickTitle: Run a routine from the bottom
translations.tourQuickLead: The strip holds your routines. One tap runs one — no menus, no settings.
translations.tourAddLead: Use Add to place clocks, weather, status cards or your own device groups on the dashboard.
translations.tourEditLead: Use Edit, then the left and right arrows to arrange widgets. Finish editing when the layout feels right.
translations.tourWidgetsLead: Widgets scroll sideways in their own area while the top controls stay in place.
translations.tourMenuTitle: Everything else is in the menu
translations.tourMenuLead: This button opens the menu: Home, Devices, Automations, Connections, Settings, plus theme, language and sign out.
translations.deviceHintLead: Tap Add device, put the nearby Zigbee product into pairing mode and wait for Villa Bridge to find it.
translations.haLead: Connect Home Assistant to the same MQTT broker, then enable discovery when you are ready to publish the devices.
translations.haStepOne: In Home Assistant, open Settings → Devices & services → Add integration.
translations.haStepTwo: Select MQTT and enter the broker address shown here.
translations.haStepThree: Enter the protocol and credentials exactly as shown. Leave username and password blank when authentication is not required.
translations.haStepFour: Keep the discovery prefix as “homeassistant”, then enable discovery below.
translations.discoveryConfirm: Change Home Assistant discovery and restart Villa Bridge?
translations.discoveryEnabledLive: Home Assistant publishing service started. MQTT stayed online.
translations.discoveryDisabledLive: Home Assistant publishing service stopped. MQTT stayed online.
translations.haStableIpTitle: Keep the tablet IP address stable
translations.haIpDynamic: Your router may assign a different address after a restart.
translations.haDhcpReservation: Recommended: create a DHCP reservation in your router. In the current Wi-Fi network details, find the MAC address Android uses for this network, then bind that MAC to the current IP.
translations.haStaticAlternative: Alternative: Android Settings → Network & Internet → Internet → current network → pencil/advanced → IP settings → Static. Keep gateway, DNS and subnet values consistent with the router network.
translations.haIpNotMqtt: This changes the tablet’s network address; it is different from editing the MQTT URL in Villa Bridge.
translations.wifiSettingsAndroidOnly: Wi-Fi settings can only be opened from the Android app.
translations.runtimeLead: Stop Zigbee, MQTT and Matter together when this tablet must release the home network.
translations.runtimeStopConfirm: Stop Zigbee, MQTT and Matter on this tablet? The app will keep a Start button available.
translations.tabletCareLead: Keep the tablet awake and running as the home controller.
translations.batteryGuardLead: Android may put sleeping apps to sleep for good. Exempting Villa Bridge keeps Zigbee, MQTT and Matter alive while the screen is off. You can refuse, and you can take it back later.
translations.batteryGuardAndroidOnly: Background protection can only be changed from the Android app.
translations.watchdogHealthy: The system has not crashed since the last stable start.
translations.watchdogRestarts: Restarted {count} of {max} times. The next attempt waits {seconds} s; the last exit code was {code}.
translations.watchdogExhausted: Automatic restart gave up after {count} failures in a row. Fix the cause, then start the system again from the app.
translations.screenIdleHelp: The clock and date screen appears after this long on the home view, and a touch brings the panel back.
translations.screenDimEnabledLabel: Dim the screen while the screensaver shows
translations.screenBrightnessSystemLead: With permission, the slider in the menu writes the tablet’s own brightness setting — the same value you see in Android settings, and a change made there comes back here. Without it Villa Bridge still works, but the slider only dims its own screen.
translations.screenBrightnessNeedsPermission: Right now this only dims Villa Bridge’s own screen. Allow it to write the tablet’s brightness setting to change the device itself.
translations.screenBrightnessAutoOff: Automatic brightness was switched off so this slider can hold its value.
translations.screenBrightnessAndroidOnly: The tablet brightness setting can only be changed from the Android app.
translations.screenNightActive: Night brightness is in effect right now.
translations.screenPolicyFailed: The screen setting could not be applied: {error}
translations.debugModeLead: Keep a short, privacy-safe list of recent system errors while testing.
translations.deviceNetworkEventsLead: Joins, drops and deletions stay here even after a restart.
translations.selfHealingLead: When a device announces itself again, refresh its reporting setup automatically. Unreachable devices are never polled.
translations.addWidgetLead: Choose compact widgets for the information you want to see at a glance.
translations.summaryWidgetLead: Which devices are reachable, plus the latest button presses and safety changes.
translations.deviceRoomLead: Pick the room {name} belongs to. Skip it and the device waits in the “No room” card.
translations.deviceRoomNone: No rooms yet — create the first one below.
translations.roomFilterEmpty: No devices in this room yet.
translations.roomSuggestHint: Pick a suggestion or type your own name.
translations.deleteGroupWarning: “{name}” will be removed from every device you sign in from.
translations.deleteGroupNote: The devices themselves stay untouched — only the room disappears.
translations.groupsMigrated: {count} rooms moved to the server and are now shared across your devices.
translations.groupsMigrationFailed: Rooms could not be moved to the server: {error}
translations.visibilitySaveFailed: Your show/hide choice could not be saved to the server: {error}
translations.visibilityLoadFailed: Show/hide choices could not be loaded from the server, showing the last known ones: {error}
translations.favoritesWidgetLead: The devices you starred, gathered on one card.
translations.favoritesEmpty: No favourites yet. Tap the star on a device page, or in Edit mode on any tile.
translations.favoritesFull: Favourites are full ({count} at most). Remove one before adding another.
translations.favoritesSaveFailed: Your favourites could not be saved to the server: {error}
translations.favoritesLoadFailed: Favourites could not be loaded from the server, showing the last known ones: {error}
translations.groupDialogLead: Give the widget a simple name, then choose its controls.
translations.groupDeviceGate: First give the group a name — pick a suggestion or type your own. The devices appear right after.
translations.groupNoControls: No available controls in this group.
translations.groupNoAvailableControls: Add a controllable device before creating a group.
translations.confirmReconnectedNameLead: This known device reconnected. Keep its current name or enter a new one.
translations.zigbeeToolsLead: Advanced pairing and recovery tools stay here for administrators.
translations.installCodePlaceholder: Install code or Zigbee QR value
translations.zigbeeChannelLead: Changing the channel can disconnect devices and requires a service restart.
translations.zigbeeChannelConfirm: Change the Zigbee channel from {from} to {to}? Battery devices may not follow the change and could require re-pairing. Continue only if you understand this risk.
translations.lowBatteryThresholdLead: Create an alert when a battery reaches this percentage (5–50%).
translations.networkGraphLead: Devices are arranged by their role. Line colour and thickness show link quality.
translations.updateAvailable: A firmware update is available. Schedule it when the device can stay powered.
translations.noUpdateAvailable: The device is already up to date.
translations.updateScheduled: Firmware update scheduled for the device's next check.
translations.zigbeeGroupsLead: Create a real Zigbee group so several lights react together with one radio command.
translations.noZigbeeGroupsLead: Name a room or area above, create the group, then add its lights.
translations.directBindingLead: Connect a button directly to a light or group. It keeps working while Villa Bridge is offline. Automatic reporting links to the coordinator stay hidden.
translations.noBindingsLead: Choose the source and target endpoints above to create one.
translations.simpleLinkPathLead: Let a button run a light directly. It works even when the system is off.
translations.rulePathLead: Run it by time, by a sensor or by a device state.
translations.simpleLinkStepOneLead: Choose the button or remote that should start it.
translations.simpleLinkStepTwoLead: Pick a room, then choose the light or socket it should run.
translations.simpleLinkNoStarters: No buttons or remotes were found yet.
translations.simpleLinkBridgeHandoff: This remote cannot link directly; setting it up as a rule.
translations.simpleLinkNoTargets: No lights or sockets were found here.
translations.simpleLinkDirectNote: This link is created straight between the devices — it works even when the system is off.
translations.automationsEmptyLead: Start with “New automation”. You can set a time, or connect a button straight to a light.
translations.automationWhenLead: Pick the moment that starts it.
translations.automationThenLead: Choose the device, then what should happen.
translations.automationReviewLead: Read it once, then save it.
translations.automationAutoOffLead: Choose what should happen after the device turns on.
translations.automationTriggerDeviceState: When a switch or plug turns on or off
translations.automationNoTargets: No writable device property was found.
translations.automationValueBrightnessHint: You pick a percentage; the rule stores the lamp’s own unit.
translations.automationValueWarmthHint: The higher the percentage, the warmer the light.
translations.automationValueColorHint: Pick a preset color or choose your own.
translations.automationValueGenericHint: The value follows the range and step exposed by the device.
translations.automationFollowHint: The value from {device} is applied to this target.
translations.automationAgentBarNote: An assistant changed these rules. You can put them back the way they were.
translations.automationActionLead: Choose what you want to do with this automation.
translations.automationDuplicateReady: Copy ready — change the name and devices, then save. The copy starts switched off.
translations.automationNoButtons: No device with buttons was found.
translations.automationNoSensors: No suitable device was found here.
translations.deviceButtonLearnHint: Press a button on the device to see which one it is.
translations.automationPressToLearn: Not sure which button? Press it and the last press shows up here.
translations.automationButtonUnprovenGroup: Devices not seen sending a press yet
translations.automationButtonUnproven: this device has not sent a button signal yet
translations.automationButtonUnprovenWarning: This device may not send button signals, so the rule may never run. Press a button on the device and check that it shows up here.
translations.automationButtonStateAlternative: This device turns on and off like a switch or plug. Would you like to build the rule that way instead?
translations.automationPathTitle: How do you want to set this up?
translations.automationPathLead: Pick one of the two ways.
translations.automationClearDevice: Clear the device and show the list again
translations.automationCloseConfirm: Close the wizard? What you filled in is not saved.
translations.automationNeedTrigger: Pick what should start the rule.
translations.automationNeedEvent: Pick which button or event starts it.
translations.automationNeedTarget: Pick the device it should run.
translations.automationNeedMap: Pick at least one thing to do.
translations.automationTargetLead: Choose the device it should control.
translations.automationMapLead: Choose what happens when it turns on and when it turns off.
translations.automationMapLaterHint: You will decide what happens in each case after you pick the device to run.
translations.automationSummaryMap: When {device} turns on, {target} will {onAction}, and when it turns off it will {offAction}.
translations.automationLoopWarning: This is the very channel that starts the automation, so it cannot start itself. Pick another target.
translations.automationAutoOffTitle: Should it turn itself off later?
translations.automationAutoOffAfterLabel: How long after the rule runs should it turn off?
translations.automationAutoOffIdleWaitLabel: How long to wait after motion stops?
translations.automationAutoOffIdleHint: New motion starts the countdown over. If your sensor never reports that motion stopped, pick the timed option instead.
translations.automationAutoOffAfterHint: Running the rule again starts the countdown over. If you touch the light yourself meanwhile (panel, Alexa, Apple Home or the wall switch), the automatic turn-off is cancelled.
translations.automationManualSentence: When its button is tapped, {device} will run.
translations.automationAutoOffNeverLine: It will not turn itself off
translations.automationAutoOffNeverSub: It stays on until you or another rule turns it off
translations.automationAutoOffIdleSub: It turns off after motion stops; new motion starts the countdown over
translations.automationAutoOffAfterSub: It turns off this long after the rule runs
translations.automationNameHint: Leave it blank to use the name above.
translations.automationSunOffsetHint: Minus is before, plus is after. 0:00 means exactly then.
translations.automationMapSunLead: Choose what happens at sunset and at sunrise.
translations.automationSummarySunMap: At sunset {target} will {onAction}, and at sunrise it will {offAction}.
translations.automationThresholdHint: It runs once, the moment the value crosses the line.
translations.automationCondLead: Add a condition, or leave it to run every time.
translations.automationCondTimeSub: For example only in the evening.
translations.automationCondState: Only when a device is in a state
translations.automationCondStateSub: For example only when the hallway light is off.
translations.automationCondStateFor: Only when a device has been in a state for a while
translations.automationCondStateForSub: For example only when nobody has moved for 5 minutes.
translations.automationCondMeasure: Only when a measurement is above or below a value
translations.automationCondMeasureSub: For example only when the light level is below 30.
translations.automationCondNoMeasureDevices: No device here reports a numeric measurement yet.
translations.automationCondNoMeasure: This device does not report a numeric measurement.
translations.automationCondOvernightHint: A range may cross midnight: 22:00 → 06:00 means all night.
translations.automationCondSunLocked: Enter your home location to use sunrise and sunset here.
translations.automationCondThresholdRow: {reading} is above or below a value
translations.automationCondThresholdHint: It passes if the value meets this the moment the rule runs.
translations.automationCondFreshTitle: How recent must the reading be?
translations.automationCondFreshHint: A value that fits is not the same as a value that is current: a sensor whose reading never changes can be reporting a months-old number. With a window set, the condition passes only if the device reported that reading inside it. This is kept in memory only — right after a server restart nothing has been reported yet, so a rule with a window stays blocked until the sensor speaks again.
translations.automationCondNoDevices: No device here reports a state that can be used as a condition.
translations.automationCondNoState: This device does not report a state that can be used as a condition.
translations.automationNeedCondValue: Pick the state to look for.
translations.automationNeedCondRange: Start and end cannot be the same.
translations.automationWaitLead: Should it run the moment it triggers, or wait a little first?
translations.automationWaitHint: 0:00 = run right away. The dial shows minutes:seconds, up to 5:00 (300 seconds).
translations.automationActionDelaySub: Pause before the next action in this list.
translations.automationActionGroup: Turn a group on or off
translations.automationActionGroupSub: One radio command for the whole group.
translations.automationActionSceneSub: Bring back a scene stored in a group.
translations.automationActionNoScenes: This group has no stored scene yet.
translations.automationDelayHint: A pause between two actions: 1 to 300 seconds. A pending wait is lost if the system restarts.
translations.automationNeedRealAction: A rule needs at least one real action next to the waits.
translations.automationRunsOlderThanLog: This rule ran before this version; the log has only just started.
translations.automationReasonBusy: The previous run had not finished.
translations.automationReasonLocationMissing: The home location is not set, so sunrise and sunset cannot be worked out.
translations.automationReasonSunUnavailable: The sun does not cross the horizon here today.
translations.automationReasonNonNumericValue: The reported value was not a number.
translations.automationReasonNoPreviousValue: There was no earlier value to compare with.
translations.automationReasonRepeatSuppressed: The same event repeated too quickly.
translations.automationReasonStopped: The system stopped before the remaining actions ran.
translations.automationReasonUnsupportedAction: This action type is not supported.
translations.automationReasonActionFailed: The device did not accept the command.
translations.automationReasonAutoOffCanceled: Automatic switch-off was canceled because the target changed.
translations.automationRunsUnavailable: The run log could not be read.
translations.homeLocationLead: Sunrise and sunset triggers need to know where the house is. Nothing is sent anywhere; the times are worked out on this device.
translations.homeLocationMissing: No location set yet, so sunrise and sunset triggers cannot run.
translations.homeLocationReadOnly: Only an administrator can change this.
translations.automationCondForOpen: … and it has been this way for a while
translations.automationCondForLabel: How long must it have been this way?
translations.automationCondForHint: This is a test for running: the rule runs only if the state has held this long without a break. Don't confuse it with “turn off afterwards” in the action step — that one describes what happens after the rule runs. If the server restarts, the clock starts over.
translations.automationCondStateNotForLine: Only if {device} has not been {event} for {duration}
translations.automationCondAboveForLine: Only if {device} {reading} has been above {value} for {duration}
translations.automationCondBelowForLine: Only if {device} {reading} has been below {value} for {duration}
translations.automationCondBetweenForLine: Only if {device} {reading} has been between {from} and {to} for {duration}
translations.automationCondPickWhy: Only devices that report a state appear here. If a device is missing, it has no state that can be read as a condition.
translations.automationTrigForOpen: … and it has been this way for a while
translations.automationTrigForLabel: How long should it stay this way?
translations.automationTrigForHint: The rule runs once the state has stayed this way without a break for that long. If the state changes and comes back, it starts counting again. Do not confuse this with “turn off afterwards” in the action step — that describes what happens after the rule runs. If the server restarts, the duration starts from zero.
translations.deviceLostLead: The device dropped off the network before setup finished, so nothing was saved. Put it back into pairing mode and try again.
translations.deviceRemovedLead: You removed this device a moment ago, so its settings could not be saved. Add it again from the start when you are ready.
translations.pairingRemovedWarning: This device was removed a moment ago. If pairing does not finish, wait a minute and try again.
translations.pairingDeviceWait: The device briefly lost its connection. Waiting for it to come back…
translations.pairingDeviceReturned: The device is back. Setup continues where it left off.
translations.agentAccessLead: Give your own AI assistant a token so it can read the home over the MCP endpoint. A token never expires and is shown only once, right after you create it.
translations.agentTokenRevealLead: This is the only time the token is shown. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
translations.agentTokenCopyFailed: The token could not be copied. Select it and copy by hand.
translations.agentTokenRevokeConfirm: Revoke the token “{name}”? The assistant using it loses access immediately.
translations.timeZoneInvalid: Choose a valid IANA time zone such as Europe/London.
translations.homeLocationTimeZoneVerify: Please verify the migrated time zone.
translations.appearancePackageLead: Choose a material family and tune fixed or solar colours without changing the sun behaviour.
translations.systemSectionLead: Restart the radio or the whole service when the home stops responding. Names, rooms, automations and the Zigbee network are never touched.
translations.coordinatorRestartLead: Resets the radio chip inside the coordinator. Devices stay paired and the network keeps its key.
translations.coordinatorRestartHint: If this does not help, unplug the coordinator for 10 seconds and plug it back in.
translations.coordinatorRestartConfirm: Restart the coordinator's radio chip? Zigbee devices will not respond for about half a minute.
translations.coordinatorRestartRunning: Asking the coordinator to restart its radio…
